quick.summary: Why a test with six metrics can fool you, and what to decide before it starts.
quick.takeaway: Before the test: one metric, and what counts as a win.

beats.line: Our test tracked six metrics. One went up. Did we win?
Which one did you expect to move before it started?
We never said. We just watched them all.
Then one going up can be luck. Check enough numbers, and one often will.

board.text: 6 metrics: one may move by chance

beats.line: Isn’t watching more metrics a way to learn more?
Watch them, yes. But decide the winner before you look.
Write one sentence first. What change, which metric, how much.
The shorter form will raise sign ups by at least two points.
That’s the one. Today’s lucky rise becomes the idea for your next test.

quiz.question: Why decide the main metric before an A/B test starts?
options: So a lucky move in some metric is not mistaken for a win
quiz.explanation: With many metrics, one often moves by chance; a metric chosen in advance avoids being fooled.

quiz.question: If any of the metrics you watched went up, the test was a success.
quiz.explanation: Checking many numbers makes a chance rise likely. The win is judged on the metric chosen before the test.
